 How K-beauty, cultural immersion propelled South Korea past 20 million visitors
 Forget whirlwind bus tours and duty-free checklists. Today’s travelers are flying to Seoul and beyond to book personal color consultations, curate skincare routines and live out the scenes they stream at home
 International visitors receive skincare consultations at an Olive Young store in Seongsu, Seoul, on May 13, 2025 (Photo by Hyeong Taek Im) 
 2 
 2026-11-13 11:13:51
 Travel & Leisure 
On any given afternoon in Seoul’s trendsetting neighborhoods, from the flagship skincare boutiques of Seongsu, dubbed the Brooklyn of the South Korean capital, to the dermatology clinics of Gangnam, the soundscape is distinctly global. Travelers clutching baskets of snail-mucin serums and custom-blended lip tints are swapping traditional sightseeing checklists for something far more personal, especially an immersive dive into the local lifestyle.
 Jongwoo Cheon edited this article.
